Short answer: Yes — Ireland’s standard VAT rate is 23% as of today (September 4, 2026), and that standard rate is the rate that normally applies to digital/electronic services supplied in Ireland. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/current-VAT-rates.aspx?utm_source=openai))

A couple of quick caveats:
- Recent Budget changes (effective 2026) changed some hospitality/hairdressing rates to 9% but these are specific sectors and do not affect digital/electronic services. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/corporate/press-office/budget-information/previous-years/2026/budget-summary.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- If you sell digital services to customers in other EU countries, VAT is generally charged at the customer’s country rate under the cross‑border B2C rules (that’s a separate matter if your pricing PDF covers non‑Irish customers). If you want, I can pull the specific Revenue guidance on cross‑border digital services for wording to add to your document. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/current-VAT-rates.aspx?utm_source=openai))

If you’d like, upload the pricing PDF and I’ll check the exact line(s) and suggest a short updated wording or a citation you can paste into the document.
